cues: Wisdom is needed in private life too: in choosing ends, and in freedom from personal prejudice.
Even a noble end can be unwise if it is impossible: those who spent their lives seeking the philosopher's stone and the elixir of life wasted them.
Then a humble case: Mr A and Mr B hate each other.
Ask A, and you get an appalling list of B's vices; ask B, an exactly similar list about A. Tell each what the other says, and at first the hatred grows.
But with patience you may persuade each that the other has only the normal share of human wickedness, and then you have instilled some fragment of wisdom.
